summary: Iteration 7 validation of (a) employee RBAC at router level via block_employee dependency and (b) WebSocket path move to /api/ws/locations + geolocation error downgrade. Backend: 40/40 pytest cases pass — 12 blocked endpoints return 403 for both employee accounts, 3 allowed endpoints return 200, admin/data_entry/sales unaffected (regression intact), WS connect on /api/ws/locations succeeds. Frontend: all 5 logins succeed; geolocation error successfully downgraded from console.error to console.warn ('Location tracking unavailable: User denied Geolocation'); data_entry users still do NOT see product-attachments-section (regression intact, count=0).

minor.issue: Endpoint advertised in scope does not exist; actual prefix used is /api/master-data/{categories,brands,divisions,...}. Test was adjusted to use /api/master-data/categories which correctly returns 403 for employees.

ui_bugs.issue: Employee 'Rajesh' lands on /dashboard and is shown aggregate widgets (Total Users 19, Total Activities 11, Total Leads 17, Project Value BD103,250, Team Overview / Activities Status). Sidebar correctly hides admin menus, but the stats area still renders pre-populated numbers despite /api/dashboard/stats returning 403. Source of those numbers is likely cached/static fallbacks or hard-coded — should be confirmed and hidden, OR employee should be redirected to /daily-tasks on login.

integration_issues.issue: Transient warning 'WebSocket is closed before the connection is established.' on initial load before the second connect succeeds with 'WebSocket connected'. Not a regression and final state is connected, but suggests a race when navigating during connect.

action_items: (Optional) Decide policy: either redirect role==='employee' to /daily-tasks on login OR conditionally render the dashboard widgets so employees do not see Total Users / Leads / Activities counts on /dashboard.
(Optional) Investigate transient 'WebSocket is closed before the connection is established' warning on first page load; possibly debounce socket creation until auth/page is ready.
critical_code_review_comments: block_employee dependency in /app/backend/rbac.py performs an extra DB lookup per request just to read role; consider caching role in JWT/auth dependency to avoid an additional Mongo round-trip on every gated request.
rbac.py uses a function-local 'from server import db' inside every dependency to avoid a circular import — this works but is fragile; a shared db.py module would be cleaner.
Frontend dashboard widgets are still visible to employee role on /dashboard even though sidebar links are hidden; client-side route guard / redirect is missing for employees.
ProductsEnhanced.js (1183 lines) still exceeds 700-line guideline (carried over from iter6) — recommend splitting.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (5/5 logins, attachments gating regression, WS new path, geolocation downgrade all verified)

test_credentials: All five required credentials verified working. sales role tested with sales@test.com/sales123 (the one in /app/memory/test_credentials.md is agent@test.com/agent123 which is a different sales seed). Suggest adding sales@test.com/sales123 to test_credentials.md.
seed_data_creation: None; pytest tests do not create persistent seed data (sales test uses GET only).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 7 confirmed backend RBAC + WS path fixes. Pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_role_access_iter7.py covers employee 403 on 12 endpoints, employee 200 on 3 endpoints, non-employee regression, WS new path connect (and informational old-path probe). Use BASE_URL from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Outstanding (not regressions): (1) employee /dashboard widgets still show aggregate numbers — frontend redirect/guard recommended; (2) transient WS open/close warning on first load.
rca of the issue: N/A — this iteration validated fixes rather than triaging a bug. (a) employee router-level guard implemented via block_employee dependency injected into 12 routers — all employee GETs now return 403 with detail 'Employees only have access to Daily Tasks'. (b) WS endpoint registered at @app.websocket('/api/ws/locations') so it routes through the K8s ingress (which only forwards /api/* to backend:8001); frontend LocationContext.js builds wsUrl as backendUrl.replace('http','ws') + '/api/ws/locations'; verified open via Playwright (WS_OPEN logged) and Python websockets client (200 OK upgrade). (c) Geolocation error downgraded to console.warn — confirmed via console capture: 'Location tracking unavailable: User denied Geolocation' is now at warn level, no error-level Geolocation logs.
